summary: Simplified Developer, Reviewer, and Documentation personas by offloading dedicated responsibilities to the new Security Auditor and Release Engineer agents.
Added 'Declare All Artifacts' constraint to developer-strict-constraints.md — instructs developers to list ALL modified files in artifacts.files_modified when completing a pipeline.
Removed 'Security & Performance' Review Dimension from 6-reviewer.md — replaced with 'Performance' only (security belongs to Security Auditor).
Added Security Auditor note to 6-reviewer.md Review Dimensions: 'Security concerns are handled by the Security Auditor in a dedicated pipeline stage.'
Removed 'security vulnerabilities, or' from reviewer FAIL criteria — decision logic now focuses on bugs and maintainability concerns.
Verified developer-strict-constraints.md contained no Security Auditor-specific constraints (criteria 3 already met).
Verified reviewer-operational-protocol.md contained no security review steps (criteria 6 already met).

Build verified: node scripts/build-personas.js --suite all --strict produced 48 personas with zero errors. --check confirmed all output is up-to-date.

comments.note: developer-strict-constraints.md: Artifact declaration guidance was added as a new constraint bullet. This addresses a gap where developers could complete pipelines without fully declaring modified files — common in persona-centric workspaces where ancillary files (e.g., generated outputs) are easy to overlook.

6-reviewer.md: The 'Security & Performance' Review Dimension was cleanly split — Security removed (now owned by Security Auditor), Performance retained as its own bullet. This makes the boundary between Reviewer and Security Auditor responsibilities explicit.

Criteria 1, 3, 6, and 7 were already satisfied in the current source files — no security annotation duties in Developer, no security constraints in developer-strict-constraints.md, no security review steps in reviewer-operational-protocol.md, no changelog/release notes in 8-documentation.md. This suggests Plan 1 may have already partially simplified these personas, or the WP was written defensively. Either way, the current state is correct and clean.

Documentation persona has no changelog/release notes duties.

comments.note: 6-reviewer.md mission statement (line 7) retains the word 'secure' in 'ensure the code is maintainable, secure, and follows architectural best practices.' This is a general quality descriptor rather than an active review instruction — the Review Dimensions explicitly redirect security to the Security Auditor with a callout note. Not a blocker, but a future revision could align the mission language with the new role boundaries (e.g., swap 'secure' for 'well-architected').

developer-strict-constraints.md is correctly scoped — only included via {{> developer-strict-constraints}} in personas/ledger/src/content/3-developer.md; no other persona references it. The new 'Declare All Artifacts' constraint is clean and precise.

summary: WP-005 PASS. Changes to developer-strict-constraints.md and 6-reviewer.md are surgical, correct, and internally consistent. All 8 acceptance criteria confirmed against source files and verified generated outputs.

Reviewer Review Dimensions now list exactly 4 criteria (Maintainability, Best Practices, Performance, Future Context) — Security cleanly removed and delegated via a callout note. FAIL criteria correctly trimmed. No template syntax regressions (48 personas build clean).
Developer artifact declaration constraint is well-worded and positioned logically in the constraints list. No over-engineering; all changes are minimal and targeted per the WP spec.

One non-blocking observation recorded: mission statement in 6-reviewer.md still contains 'secure' — general quality descriptor, not an active review instruction, but semantically diverges from the redefined Review Dimensions.

comments.note: 6-reviewer.md mission statement (line 7) retains 'secure' in 'ensure the code is maintainable, secure, and follows architectural best practices.' The Review Dimensions have been correctly updated to remove the Security criterion, and a callout note makes delegation to the Security Auditor explicit. However, the mission statement now has a semantic gap — it names 'secure' as a goal but the Review Dimensions no longer include it as an active criterion. A future polish pass should align the mission language (e.g., replace 'secure' with 'well-architected') to eliminate any ambiguity about what the Reviewer is responsible for.

developer-strict-constraints.md: Constraint ordering is logical. 'Declare All Artifacts' sits between 'Error Handling' and 'No GIT write operations', which groups it with process/behavioral constraints rather than code-quality constraints. Positioning is appropriate for the semantics of the instruction.

The reviewer FAIL criteria change ('security vulnerabilities, or' removed) is a clean one-phrase excision. The resulting sentence — 'problems that would cause bugs or significant maintainability concerns' — reads naturally with no grammatical artifacts. Good surgical precision from the Developer.
